critique: Watcher stopped itself correctly. At poll 43 (~03:51 MST) the gh keyring token read back invalid, check.mjs exit 2, and the watcher reported 'gh UNAVAILABLE - not reporting no new reviews' and stopped instead of logging 43 clean polls and a 44th silent zero. That is step 1 behaving exactly as designed, and it is the first time the silent-zero guard has actually fired in this loop's life. Auth recovered on its own by 07:58 (scopes unchanged: gist, read:org, repo, workflow); catch-up check confirms 0 open PRs, so the ~4h blind window had nothing to miss. Relaunched the watcher.

adjustment: First live firing of the step-1 silent-zero guard: a transient gh keyring invalidation is a real failure mode on this machine, not just a theoretical one. The guard stopped the watcher rather than degrading it into a false all-clear - correct, but it means an outage silently ends the watch until a human notices. Worth deciding at the retrospective whether the watcher should retry a few times before giving up, since the failure here was transient and self-healing.
The blind window was harmless only because the fleet was at 0 open PRs. With an open PR it would have been a real gap, compounded by check.mjs's silent baselining of a first-seen PR.
